purpose: Tasimelteon is used to treat Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder, a condition where your internal body clock does not stay on a normal 24-hour cycle. It is especially common in people who are totally blind. It helps reset your sleep schedule so you can fall asleep and wake up at more consistent, normal times.
how_it_works: Your body has a natural internal clock that tells you when to sleep and wake up. Tasimelteon works by attaching to the same receptors in your brain that respond to melatonin, which is your body's natural sleep hormone. By doing this, it helps to gradually reset and synchronize your body clock to a regular 24-hour schedule.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, dizziness, unusual dreams or nightmares, upper respiratory infections like a stuffy or runny nose, and elevated liver enzymes. You may also feel drowsy, so be careful when driving or doing activities that require alertness.
warnings: Do not drive or operate heavy machinery after taking this medication, especially until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Avoid taking tasimelteon with other sleep medications, alcohol, or sedatives unless your doctor approves. Do not take it with fluvoxamine (an antidepressant) as this combination can increase side effects significantly. This medication is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 20 mg taken by mouth once per night, about 30 minutes before your target bedtime. Take it at the same time every night for the best results. It may take weeks to months before you notice the full benefit, so be patient and keep taking it as directed.
